Duensing has made an appearance in two games against the Yankees this season, pitching a combined one inning in those outings. He gave up one earned run and two walks in those appearances. It is his only earned run of the season. Duensing has allowed only two hits and has four strikeouts through 7 1/3 innings pitched this year.
away_pitcher_note: The Yankees did not announce who will be on the mound in the bottom of the sixth when they resume Tuesday's game on Wednesday, but Mitre is a likely candidate. The right-hander made two starters earlier this month, including one against the Twins on May 16. He allowed one run on four hits in five innings but did not get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: After rain suspended Tuesday's game, Duensing will take the mound when the game resumes on Wednesday. Duensing has made an appearance in two games against the Yankees this season, pitching a combined one inning in those outings. He gave up one earned run and two walks in those appearances. It is his only earned run of the season. Duensing has allowed only two hits and has four strikeouts through 7 1/3 innings pitched this year.
away_pitcher_note: The Yankees did not announce who will be on the mound in the bottom of the sixth when they resume Tuesday's game on Wednesday, but Mitre is a likely candidate. The right-hander made two starters earlier this month, including one against the Twins on May 16. He allowed one run on four hits in five innings but did not get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano will see familiar faces when he takes the mound Wednesday against the Yankees. This will be the second time Liriano faces New York in his past three starts. He gave up three runs on nine hits through six innings the last time he faced the team on May 15. That loss was followed by another loss in Boston where Liriano gave up five runs on five hits and two walks. The left-hander is on a three-game losing streak and is looking to rebound on home turf. After snapping his home winning streak against Baltimore earlier this month, he is looking to regain his composure at home and even his record against the Yankees this season. Liriano is 4-3 with a 4.04 ERA this season. He has 52 strikeouts through 52 2/3 innings. He had seven strikeouts in his May 15 outing against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte had by far his worst start of the season last Thursday against the Rays, surrendering seven runs (six earned) in five innings en route to his first loss of the season. It was also Pettitte's first loss in 14 starts dating back to October 2009. Pettitte was fabulous when he faced the Twins on May 15, shutting them out on two hits over 6 1/3 innings. The left-hander is 10-5 with a 3.53 ERA in 20 career starts against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn had a solid outing against the Brewers backed up by a strong offensive effort by the Twins. The only runs he gave up came on a three-run blast by Carlos Gomez in the seventh inning. Blackburn lasted 7 1/3 innings in that game, the fifth time this season he has made it to at least the seventh inning. In that game, he said he kept his pitches down to force the Brewers to hit grounders and gave up seven hits in that outing. Blackburn is set to face the Yankees for the second time in as many weeks. The right-hander recorded the only win against the Yankees in the previous three-game series. He gave up three runs and had four strikeouts in that contest. Blackburn is on a four-game winning streak and has an ERA of 4.50.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez was nothing short of phenomenal in his return to the rotation last Friday, holding the Mets to a single hit in six innings before leaving the game with a bruised finger incurred on a bunt. Vazquez had only 70 pitches at the time. It was the second straight good start and third consecutive impressive outing for Vazquez, who also pitched well in Detroit and in a rare relief role against the Red Sox. In 16 career starts against the Twins, Vazquez is 6-6 with a 5.11 ERA. He has not faced Minnesota since 2008 when, as a member of the White Sox, he won two of three decisions over the Twins despite a 6.61 ERA. Vazquez struggles in particular with Justin Morneau, who is 14-for-40 with six home runs off the right-hander.

Carmona gave up five runs on seven hits with two walks and four strikeouts over six innings in his start against the Reds on Saturday. Two of the runs were unearned, as the Indians played sloppy defense behind him. Still, Carmona was not at his sharpest. His slider was flat early in the ballgame, and he struggled against the Reds' left-handed hitters. Carmona has a 2.63 ERA over his past four starts. He's lasted at least six innings in eight of nine starts and thrown a quality start seven times.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia takes the mound looking to snap his string of winless starts on Saturday. The lefty allowed six runs (five earned) on 10 hits to the Mets on May 23, a five-inning losing effort. Sabathia has not won since May 3 at Baltimore, a span of four starts, although he was one out shy of qualifying for a victory on May 8 when rain forced him from a 14-3 win over the Red Sox. Sabathia is 1-0 with a 2.84 ERA in two career starts against his former team.
away_pitcher_note: Huff wasn't perfect in his start against the Reds on Sunday, but he was much improved over previous efforts and might have calmed some talk about him possibly getting sent down to the Minors. He ended a streak of five straight starts with a loss. He allowed three runs on six hits with a walk and four strikeouts over six innings. He served up two home run balls but nevertheless gave his team a chance to win and earned his first victory since April 15.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett gets the nod on Sunday, looking for his second consecutive win. Burnett hurled five innings of scoreless, three-hit ball on May 25 at Minnesota, but threw only 75 pitches before rain forced the game to be suspended heading to the sixth. Derek Jeter homered to make a winner of Burnett, who is 2-2 in five May starts. He is 1-4 with a 6.69 ERA in six career starts vs. Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson remains in the Indians' rotation, for now. But suffice to say he's on shaky ground, given his results in a starting role the past two seasons. He hasn't notched a win since Aug. 20, 2009, losing 11 consecutive decisions. That's just two shy of a team record. He has a 1.89 WHIP and a .386 average against when facing lefties. He was roughed up for five runs on nine hits in four innings in a loss to the White Sox on Monday. The Indians might end up moving Aaron Laffey from the bullpen to the rotation. But for now, they're sticking with Masterson, one of three pitchers acquired in last summer's Victor Martinez trade with the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte will get the ball as the Yankees wrap up their set with Cleveland on Monday. He was excellent on May 26 at Minnesota, holding the Twins to two runs on eight hits in eight innings, walking none and striking out four in a 94-pitch winning effort. Pettitte is 3-1 with a 3.33 ERA in four starts this month, with his only loss coming against the Rays on May 20. Pettitte is 7-8 with a 4.41 ERA in 19 career starts vs. Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot righted himself after a shaky outing against the Royals with an effective and incredibly efficient effort against the White Sox on Tuesday. He needed just 77 pitches to get through seven innings in which he allowed just a pair of runs on six hits with four strikeouts. The big key was the zero walks he allowed as he used his four-pitch arsenal to pound the strike zone and get quick outs. He began to lose effectiveness in his seventh and final inning, giving up four doubles. But this was nonetheless another solid effort for Talbot, who has been a pleasant surprise in the back end of the rotation for an Indians team that acquired him in the Kelly Shoppach trade with the Rays over the winter.

home_pitcher_note: After a few encouraging outings, Vazquez took a step back in his last start in Minnesota, yielding five earned runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings. He did find his stuff a bit after a rocky first two innings before letting the game slip away a little in the sixth. At 3-5, Vazquez is the only Yankees starter with a losing record, and he has allowed five earned runs or more in four of his eight starts this season. He is 6-2 with a 4.80 ERA in 12 career starts against the Orioles, but he has not faced Baltimore since 2008.
away_pitcher_note: It has been all about the beginning of the game for Matusz in his recent outings. After lasting just 2 1/3 innings and giving up seven runs against the Rangers, he allowed another four-run first inning on Wednesday against Oakland. He settled down and retired 10 straight batters in innings 3-5, finishing with six total earned runs allowed in five innings. He gave up eight hits and walked one batter while striking out four. Matusz has started three times against the Yankees, going 1-2 with a 2.37 ERA. Since giving up three runs in six innings in a loss to the Yankees on April 29, he has lost a career-high five straight decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Hughes delivered a bounce-back performance last Friday against the Indians, completing seven innings for the fourth time in six May starts and giving up only two runs on five hits. He moved to 6-1 on the season with the 8-2 victory. The key for Hughes was his ability to finish hitters with the aid of his offspeed stuff, especially a sharp curveball. Lifetime, Hughes is 2-2 with a 5.97 ERA in nine games (six starts) against the Orioles. That includes a no-decision earlier this season in which he allowed one run on two hits in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bergesen, an Oakland native, held the A's to two runs through seven innings, retiring 14 straight at one point. But Oakland put a five-spot on the board with two outs in the eighth to ruin the right-hander's shot at a win. Still, the start was promising for Bergesen, who has had a largely up-and-down year. He will look to carry some of that momentum into Wednesday's start in New York. Bergesen lost his only start against the Yankees and has a 5.86 career ERA as a result.

home_pitcher_note: It's rare indeed to see the Yankees lose a game in which they score 11 runs; it's even rarer when they have Sabathia on the mound. Sabathia wasn't the primary culprit in the Bombers' 13-11 loss last Saturday to the Indians -- his bullpen did allow eight runs in the game -- but he chided himself afterward for keeping the Tribe in the game. Sabathia looked lights-out through the first three innings, but he labored after that, giving up five runs in six taxing innings. It was the third time in his past four starts that Sabathia surrendered five runs or more in a start, and the Yankees are 0-4 over that stretch. He is 2-0, however, against the Orioles this season, giving up a total of four runs in 15 2/3 innings in two starts. That's par for the course for Sabathia, who is a remarkable 11-1 with a 2.52 ERA in 16 career starts against Baltimore.
away_pitcher_note: And as has been the case in all 11 of his starts, Millwood was there to absorb the brunt of the Orioles' sloppy defense and lack of offensive support in Friday's 5-0 loss to Toronto. The de facto ace of the Orioles staff, Millwood allowed four earned runs over six innings -- two of which came in his final frame -- and was handed his fifth loss of the season. Millwood's 3.98 ERA is the lowest for a starter who opened the season with 11 straight winless decisions since Rick Langford had a 2.62 ERA after 11 winless starts to open the 1978 season for Oakland. He will try to buck the trend on Wednesday in New York. Millwood is 1-8 with a 6.16 ERA in nine career starts against the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Cecil was at his best in his last start against Baltimore, going eight innings and surrendering only two runs on four hits with no walks. Just when Cecil looked like he was about to falter in the sixth, giving up RBI singles to Julio Lugo and Nick Markakis, he bounced back with a quick seventh and eighth to earn his fifth victory of the season and third in a row. For such a young pitcher, Cecil has had no problem attacking the strike zone, showcasing an outstanding 40-12 strikeout-to-walk ratio. Cecil's 3.81 ERA is nothing to sneeze at, but if you remove his two-inning, eight-run performance against Texas on May 14, the left-hander's ERA would be a miniscule 2.46. Lifetime against the Yankees, Cecil is 0-1 with an 11.25 ERA over two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett delivered his second-best performance of the season on Sunday against the Indians, going eight innings and allowing only one earned run (three runs total) on five hits. With excellent command of his fastball and a wicked knuckle-curve, Burnett punched out eight Cleveland batters en route to his sixth victory of the season. He's returning to his old stomping grounds in Toronto, where he won 38 games for the Blue Jays from 2006-08. Burnett is 2-1 with a 3.34 ERA in his career against the Jays and is 22-9 lifetime at Rogers Centre.
summary: 2010-06-04 - New York Yankees (1) @ Toronto Blue Jays (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Romero bounced back from his worst outing of the season against the Angels, where he went 5 1/3 allowing seven runs on 11 hits, with a stellar complete-game performance on Sunday, as the Jays defeated the Orioles, 6-1. The left-hander only gave up six hits and issued two walks for his second complete game of the young season. Furthermore, only two of his 27 outs were recorded in the outfield, showing his ground-ball and strikeout dominance.  His seven strikeouts Sunday gives him 79 on the season, which is good for tops on the Blue Jays. Romero will go up against the powerhouse Yankees next start, whom he is 1-1 with a 5.94 ERA against over 16 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte continued his magnificent start to the season, yielding only a Jhonny Peralta solo home run in seven sparkling innings against the Indians on Monday. The left-hander improved to 6-0 with a 1.12 ERA in six starts in day games this season. Pettitte is 20-12 with a 4.21 ERA in his career against the Blue Jays, including a 15-5 mark in Toronto. He went 3-1 against them last season.
summary: 2010-06-05 - New York Yankees (2) @ Toronto Blue Jays (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Morrow was dominant in Monday's 3-2 win against the Rays, taking a no-hit bid into the sixth inning before Sean Rodriguez hit an infield single with two outs. The young right-hander, making only his 26th big league start, ended up going seven innings and allowing one earned run on three hits and two walks against one of baseball's most potent lineups. Unlike past outings, Morrow was not reliant upon blowing the ball past hitters, as he utilized more of a pitch to contact philosophy, recording only one strikeout on the evening. Morrow has had more punchouts than innings in eight of his 11 starts this season. His next task will be equally as difficult, as Morrow will battle the Yankees, whom he is 1-0 with a 3.94 ERA over 16 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez took another step forward on Tuesday, dominating the Orioles over seven innings. The right-hander allowed a run on four hits and tied a season-high with seven strikeouts in picking up his fourth win of the season. He's now submitted fine starts in three of his last four. Vazquez is 4-7 with a 4.17 ERA in 14 career starts against the Blue Jays -- the last of which was in 2008. In his last four starts against Toronto, he has yielded five earned runs in 29 1/3 innings. He's had even more success at Rogers Centre, where he's 2-1 with a 1.50 ERA in five starts.
summary: 2010-06-06 - New York Yankees (4) @ Toronto Blue Jays (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Still searching for his first win of the season, the Orioles right-hander labored through his worst start of the season against New York on Thursday. He gave up two runs in the first inning, including one on a balk after losing his footing on a delivery. Two homers and four runs later he left the game with just 5 2/3 innings under his belt. The season-high six earned runs came on 10 hits and four walks, tying season highs in those categories as well. Millwood is 2-5 lifetime in 11 starts against the Yankees with a 5.15 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes sliced through the Orioles' order the last time he faced them, holding Baltimore to one run on six hits in seven innings. He also struck out seven. Hughes has lasted seven innings in five of his past seven starts, and he's recovered from that two-start blip against the Red Sox and the Mets. He has thrown a few more curveballs the last two times out, which has enabled him to finish off batters more easily. This will already be Hughes' third start against the O's this season, and he's fared well in each of the first two. He's given up two runs on eight hits in 12 2/3 vs. Baltimore, with a 1-0 record.

home_pitcher_note: In two outings since being recalled from Triple-A Norfolk, Tillman has pitched well in one start and terribly in the other. He went 5 2/3 innings in his season debut against Toronto, holding the Blue Jays' potent offense to just two runs on six hits while striking out three. But in his last outing Friday against Boston, he finished just 1 1/3 innings before interim manager Juan Samuel pulled the plug. He allowed four runs on five hits with two strikeouts. One of Tillman's 12 starts in 2009 came against the Yankees. He gave up four runs on nine hits while fanning a career-high eight hitters over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia got back on track and into the winner's column against the Orioles last week, giving up three runs on three hits in seven innings. His only trouble came with the long ball, as he surrendered homers to Adam Jones (solo) and Luke Scott (two-run). He exhibited better control of his slider and changeup throughout the afternoon. Sabathia has started three times against Baltimore already this season and has won all three. In fact, the left-hander's past three wins have all come against the O's. Sabathia has allowed just seven earned runs in 22 2/3 frames against Baltimore this season, and he is 12-1 against them in his career.

home_pitcher_note: After a stellar start to the season at Triple-A Norfolk, Arrieta will make his Major League debut against the Yankees. A highly touted righty who was drafted in the fifth round of the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, Arrieta went 6-2 with a 1.85 ERA and 64 strikeouts in 12 games (11 starts) for Norfolk. He will stay on a normal rotation for his debut, because his next scheduled start for Norfolk was Thursday as well.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett was handed his third loss of the season in Toronto on Friday, with his outing defined by three mistakes. All three were fastballs that ran back over the plate, and all three ended up in the left-field bleachers. Burnett gave up six runs in all on six hits in six innings in the Yankees' 6-1 loss. He has dominated the Orioles in his prior two starts against them in 2010, having yet to allow an earned run in 15 1/3 innings in two victories. He is 11-2 lifetime against the O's and has never lost in seven starts at Camden Yards (5-0).

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte gets the nod against his former club as the Yankees open a three-game weekend series with the Astros. He will look to tie Phil Hughes for the team lead in victories, one start after taking a no-decision in 7 2/3 innings of two-run, five-hit ball against the Blue Jays in Toronto. Pettitte won four of five decisions in May and has never faced the Astros, for whom he was 37-26 with a 3.38 ERA in 84 games from 2004-06.
away_pitcher_note: Myers has been the most dependable starter on the Astros staff this season, posting a 4-3 record with a 3.01 ERA while lasting at least six innings in each of his 12 starts, a stretch ranking as a career high. He has gotten stronger with each month of the season, posting ERAs of 3.82 in April, 2.65 in May, and 1.98 through his first two starts of June to extend his streak of quality starts to four. In his last start, Myers held the Cubs to two runs on eights hits and a walk while striking out six over 6 2/3 innings for the win. He battled through traffic, as he has through much of the season, bearing down and executing his pitches when it mattered the most.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez will start the second game of New York's three-game series with the Astros on Saturday, looking for his third consecutive victory after beating the Orioles and Blue Jays earlier this month. Vazquez hurled seven innings of one-hit, two-run ball on June 6 at Toronto, walking four and striking out nine. Vazquez is 3-5 with a 4.41 ERA in 13 career starts against Houston, including hurling seven innings of scoreless, three-hit ball in a winning effort against them in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had a strong outing in Colorado on Monday, falling to the Rockies despite recording his sixth quality start in 12 trips to the hill.  Rodriguez allowed three runs on nine hits and two walks (one intentional) in seven innings. He had command of all his pitches and was able to throw his breaking balls and changeups effectively for strikes. He pitched through a lot of traffic, but he bore down when he needed to and executed quality pitches to strand Rockies runners, getting stronger as the game progressed and retiring the last seven batters he faced, getting deep into the game and sparing the 'pen. The most damage came on a pitch he intentionally threw out of the zone, high and inside, but Clint Barmes reached for it and sent it to the left field wall to plate the game-winning runs.

home_pitcher_note: Hughes will look to win his fourth consecutive start on Sunday as the Yankees complete a three-game set with the Astros. Hughes wasn't thrilled with his stuff on June 8, but it was good enough to beat the Orioles, hurling six innings of three-run, nine-hit ball, walking none and striking out four. Hughes said that the Orioles were more aggressive, so he wasn't even elated with the zero walks. Hughes has never faced the Astros and is 0-1 with a 2.77 ERA in six Interleague appearances (one start).
away_pitcher_note: Moehler had a critical outing in Colorado, surviving a first-inning Rockies rally that put the Astros down by three, then making key adjustments and coming up with five shutout innings as his team slowly inched its way back and finally took the lead for good in the eighth inning. Moehler sensed a need to curtail Colorado's aggressive approach at the plate, and he began coming inside more to keep the Rockies honest. He ended up with his first quality start of the season, pitching six innings and allowing three runs on nine hits and three walks (one intentional) while striking out four, and his determined battling after digging himself holes was an inspiration to his teammates.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia was terrific in shutting down the Orioles last time out, but the Yankees have seen that movie before. The left-hander allowed two runs on nine hits in seven innings of a 4-2 win over Baltimore on Wednesday to earn his fourth win of the season against the O's. Sabathia hasn't beaten another team since April 16, and he's a pedestrian 2-3 against everyone besides Baltimore. He's 1-1 with a 4.35 ERA in three career regular-season starts against the Phillies and 0-2 against them in three postseason starts. In last season's World Series, Sabathia allowed five runs in 13 2/3 innings against the Phils.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay has been Halladay, which means he has been very good. He dominated the Florida Marlins on Thursday at Citizens Bank Park, yielding just one run in eight innings on just six hits and one walk. He struck out eight. The Phillies, however, couldn't muster a run against Marlins ace Josh Johnson, so Halladay took his fourth loss of the season. Halladay, like Cole Hamels, could use a little run support. Until then he needs to keep putting up zeros.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett lost his second consecutive start on Thursday in Baltimore, yielding four runs on eight hits in 6 2/3 innings. After serving up only four home runs in his first 11 starts, Burnett has matched that total in his past two outings -- a stretch of 12 2/3 innings that has seen him surrender 10 earned runs. Burnett is 5-8 with a 4.75 ERA in 17 career games against Philadelphia, and he went 1-1 in last year's World Series. The last time he faced the Phillies at Yankee Stadium, he submitted one of the finest efforts of his career, yielding just one run on four hits over seven frames while striking out nine in the Yanks' 3-1 Game 2 win.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer will try to recover from the worst start of his career in the series finale against the New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium. Moyer allowed nine runs in one-plus inning in a 12-2 loss Friday to the Boston Red Sox, his worst start since he allowed 11 runs in 3 2/3 innings on Aug. 9, 2000, against the Chicago White Sox. Moyer's ERA jumped from 3.98 to 5.03. It was the third time a Phillies starter had allowed nine or more runs in one or fewer innings since 1951. It was the first time it happened since April 20, 2006, when Ryan Madson allowed nine runs in one inning against the Washington Nationals at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: It's reached the point where Pettitte's tremendous start to the season might just be Pettitte's tremendous season. The veteran left-hander moved to 8-1 last Friday by allowing three runs (two earned) on four hits in 7 1/3 innings against his former team, the Astros. It was Pettitte's 200th victory as a member of the Yankees. In seven lifetime regular-season starts against the Phillies, Pettitte is 2-2 with a 3.67 ERA. Pettitte did earn two more victories over Philadelphia in last year's World Series, when he gave up seven runs in 11 2/3 innings in wins in Game 3 and in the clinching Game 6.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick expressed his disappointment following his start Tuesday against the Florida Marlins at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed six hits, six runs, one walk and two home runs in just five innings. Kendrick had a 2.79 ERA in his previous six starts, but as long as J.A. Happ is on the disabled list, Kendrick will need to keep proving himself. He gets a chance against a vaunted Yankees lineup at Yankee Stadium -- the first time the Phillies have played at Yankee Stadium since losing Game 6 of the 2009 World Series.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez continued his resurgence on Saturday against the Astros, holding them to three runs on six hits in seven innings to pick up his fifth win in six outings and push him over .500 for the first time this season. Vazquez struck out six and didn't walk a batter all game. Since missing a turn in the rotation in early May, Vazquez is 5-2 with a 2.93 ERA and .181 opposing batting average. One of those wins came against the Mets, who he limited to an Angel Pagan single in six innings before leaving with a bruised right index finger. Vazquez is 10-8 with a 3.24 ERA in 24 career starts against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: In danger of losing his rotation spot once John Maine returns from the disabled list, Takahashi enjoyed his first solid outing in three starts last weekend in Baltimore. Allowing one run on six hits in seven innings, Takahashi won for the second time since joining the rotation last month. His next start will provide a far greater challenge, however. Not only will Takahashi have to face the mighty Yankees, but he must do so having faced them just four weeks earlier. That may make things difficult for the 35-year-old rookie, who relies on deception.
summary: 2010-06-18 - New York Mets (4) @ New York Yankees (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Hughes picked up his ninth win on Sunday against the Astros, but both he and manager Joe Girardi thought he should have pitched better. Hughes cruised through his first five innings before laboring in the sixth, allowing a two-run single and two-run homer to the bottom of the Houston order with two outs. He ended up allowing five runs on seven hits in 5 2/3 innings. It was the first time he didn't survive the sixth since his start against the Mets on May 22. That game was his lone loss of the season, in which Hughes surrendered four runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings while also seeing the Mets foul off 41 pitches -- the most against a single pitcher in the Majors since 2005. In three career games against the Mets, Hughes is 0-1 with a 4.50 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: After defeating the Orioles last Sunday in Baltimore, Pelfrey now has recorded victories in each of his last five decisions, a span of six starts. He became the fifth pitcher in Mets history to win nine or more games in his first 10 decisions, and the first since Al Leiter in 2000. To make it 10 wins in 11 decisions, Pelfrey will have to defeat the Yankees, a team he has beaten twice in three career tries. Pelfrey has never pitched in the new Yankee Stadium.
summary: 2010-06-19 - New York Mets (3) @ New York Yankees (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia submitted a bit of a Jekyll and Hyde performance against the Phillies on Tuesday, but it was good enough to earn his seventh win of the year and first against a team other than the Orioles since April 16. Against Philadelphia, Sabathia dominated through three, labored in the fourth and fifth, and regained control in the sixth and seventh. All three runs and five hits he gave up were in those middle innings, while he retired 15 of the 16 men he faced in the other five frames. It added up to seven innings of three-run ball and his third win in as many starts after a five-start winless streak. His last loss came against the Mets on May 23, when he gave up six runs (five earned) on 10 hits in five innings. Sabathia is 2-1 with a 3.15 ERA in three lifetime starts versus the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Still not his typical flashy self, Santana nonetheless regained some of his velocity in last Tuesday's game at Cleveland. Walking two, allowing seven hits and serving up four runs, Santana lasted seven innings in total. Most encouraging was the fact that his fastball was back in the low 90s, after sitting in the mid to high 80s in his previous start. Santana will look to turn that into a better end result on Sunday at Yankee Stadium, where he was tagged for nine runs in three innings last season.
summary: 2010-06-20 - New York Mets (0) @ New York Yankees (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lopez would like to have two pitches back from his last start against the Red Sox. On both occasions he shook off catcher Chris Snyder's sign and each resulted in a ball leaving Fenway Park. The Red Sox managed four runs on those two hits alone as they went on to a 6-2 win. Lopez allowed all six of the runs on 10 hits while lasting seven innings. In his start prior to that, he allowed five runs over seven innings against the Cardinals. Three of the runs came in his final inning of work when he allowed a homer to Brendan Ryan.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett suffered his third consecutive loss in an ugly outing against the Phillies on Wednesday. He didn't survive the fourth inning for the first time this season, surrendering six runs on six hits with four walks. That included back-to-back home runs served up to Ryan Howard and Jayson Werth. Burnett has an even 9.00 ERA over those three losing starts. He is 3-2 with a 3.67 ERA in five career starts against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: After a so-so April (4.50 ERA) and a miserable May (6.08 ERA), Haren appears to finally be himself in June. In four starts this month, the D-backs ace is 2-1 with a 2.96 ERA and a 25-to-5 strikeout-to-walk ratio. After facing the Boston Red Sox on Thursday (six runs, four earned, allowed on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings), the veteran right-hander will face another American League East bully, the Yankees. In seven career starts against New York, Haren is 4-0 with a 3.77 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte lost for just the second time this season on Thursday against Philadelphia, allowing three runs (two earned) on six hits in seven innings.
